data.name: DEADLOCK
data.detailed_description:
Take a deep breath. No hacker has ever penetrated your defenses, but this foe is on a level you've never seen before. Still your employers will not tolerate failure, so you must protect your network from this invasion at all costs.

DEADLOCK is a virtual reality arcade shooter that pits you against waves of enemies who will stop at nothing to destroy you. Face down tactical troopers, flying drones and vicious attack dogs. It's kill or be killed, and to get the high score you'll need light feet, fast reflexes and a steady aim.

Features

Multiple Fire Modes

Your pistols are capable of several attacks. Fire lasers or bullets. Keep cool and pace your shots, frantically discharge until you overheat, or charge up for massive damage!

3 Different Enemies

Fight against troopers, attack dogs and flying drones.

Shield

Use your shield to protect yourself and reflect incoming fire! Keep it between yourself and the hounds if you wish to retain ownership of your jugular.

Practice Mode

One type of enemy get you every time? Practice against waves of whatever you want.

Remember to Dodge!

Enemy lasers travel slow, but not that slow! To get the high score you must dodge and weave. Watch out for your ceiling fans and furniture, they are most dangerous enemy of all!

data.short_description: Physically dodge attacks while grooving to the thumping soundtrack in this neon arcade shooter. Can you free your system from the attacks of a crazed hacker and his digital army, or will it all end in DEADLOCK...

  • Memória: 8 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970

reviews.review:
DEADLOCK is a virtual reality action title developed and published by Skunkape Interactive that emerged during the early wave of consumer VR gaming. Released in 2016, it embraces the excitement and experimentation that defined the medium's formative years. Set within a digital network overrun by malicious entities, the game casts players as the last line of defense against a hacker's destructive campaign. Its concept is straightforward, but that simplicity works to its advantage by placing the emphasis squarely on movement, reflexes, and immersion rather than elaborate storytelling or progression mechanics.

The game's biggest strength lies in how it uses VR hardware to make the player feel physically involved. Combat revolves around dodging incoming attacks with real movements, requiring players to duck, lean, and shift their bodies to avoid waves of hostile projectiles. This design gives DEADLOCK a surprisingly active feel, turning every encounter into a combination of target practice and light exercise. The pace remains consistently energetic, encouraging players to stay engaged from beginning to end. Even by today's standards, there is an undeniable appeal to a VR title that understands the value of making the player feel present inside its world.

Visually, DEADLOCK adopts a clean cybernetic style built around glowing environments and abstract digital landscapes. The game does not pursue realism, instead presenting a stylized interpretation of a computer system in crisis. Neon colors and geometric effects dominate the presentation, helping maintain visual clarity during hectic moments. Accompanying the action is an electronic soundtrack that complements the futuristic setting and enhances the arcade atmosphere. The music and visuals work together effectively, creating an experience that feels cohesive despite the project's modest production values.

The Steam description emphasizes its arcade roots, and that focus is evident throughout the experience. DEADLOCK is designed for short, repeatable sessions where chasing higher scores becomes part of the appeal. Players looking for deep customization, extensive campaigns, or evolving mechanics may find the content limited, but those seeking a quick VR showcase can still appreciate what the game offers. Its accessible structure makes it easy to understand within minutes, allowing newcomers to jump directly into the action without a lengthy learning process.

An important aspect of DEADLOCK's legacy is its Early Access background. Skunkape Interactive originally intended to expand the project through player feedback, promising additional maps, features, and gameplay improvements as development progressed. The developers openly encouraged community involvement, presenting the game as an evolving platform for experimentation. However, time has ultimately left DEADLOCK as a snapshot of an earlier era in VR development. With no significant updates in many years, the title now feels more like a historical artifact than an actively supported release.

That does not mean the game lacks value. In many ways, DEADLOCK serves as a reminder of the creativity that characterized VR's early days. Small development teams were exploring how players could interact with virtual spaces, often prioritizing immersion and physical engagement over scale. DEADLOCK succeeds in capturing that spirit. Its mechanics remain easy to appreciate, its presentation still carries a distinctive charm, and its commitment to movement-driven gameplay continues to stand out among older VR releases.

Ultimately, DEADLOCK is best viewed through the lens of its time. It is not a groundbreaking modern VR experience, nor is it an essential title for every headset owner. Instead, it is a compact arcade shooter that demonstrates the enthusiasm and ambition surrounding VR in 2016. Players interested in revisiting the medium's early years will find an enjoyable and occasionally exhilarating experience, while others may simply appreciate it as an example of how developers once envisioned the future of virtual reality gaming.

Rating: 6/10
